source.title: Monet: Mixture of Monosemantic Experts for Transformers
source.authors: Jungwoo Park; Youngjin Ahn; Kee-Eung Kim; Jaewoo Kang

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests expert specialization and knowledge localization in trained language models using routing analyses and selective expert removal, rather than reproducing the original toy-network geometry experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the superposition hypothesis and discusses SAEs, but does not measure feature-direction angles, sparsity-dependent geometric transitions, or whether toy networks drop excess features. Rows record the domain-masking MMLU results for Monet and the Gemma Scope SAE comparison; other analyses and comparators are not extracted here.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper. It cites the superposition hypothesis as motivation, builds MONET, a mixture-of-experts model with 262K experts per layer, and reports how well the method performs, chiefly how selectively expert removal unlearns a domain. Gemma Scope SAE, OLMoE and LLaMA appear only as baselines for that unlearning test. Nothing measures feature geometry, sparsity transitions or capacity competition. Nothing tests whether SAE features are complete or canonical units, or whether features are one-dimensional. Off-target degradation from SAE suppression is a selectivity and reconstruction-cost result, not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that scaling to 262,144 experts per layer, with sparse dictionary learning built into MoE pretraining, yields monosemantic experts with mutually exclusive knowledge. This allows domain, language and toxicity unlearning without degrading general performance. Gemma Scope suppression degrades broadly, which they attribute to incomplete reconstruction. They attribute OLMoE and LLaMA failures to polysemanticity.
record.recipe_differences: End-to-end pretrained MoE architecture with composed experts and routing-based expert removal; not the original toy-model intervention or geometric measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Domain masking outcomes vary by domain; SAE target-domain changes include a negligible Chemistry result and differing magnitudes across domains.

fits_no_version.finding: Suppressing domain-assigned Gemma Scope SAE features in Gemma 2 2B lowers MMLU accuracy broadly in other domains (Delta Others about -3.8 to -4.3). Splicing in the SAE alone drops benchmark averages (Table 2). The authors attribute this to incomplete SAE reconstruction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Intervening through SAE reconstructions imposes broad off-target performance costs, limiting the selectivity of SAE-feature edits.

fits_no_version.finding: About 6% of LLaMA 1.3B MLP neurons are labelled specialized per domain, versus 2.2% of MONET experts. OLMoE (64 experts) showed no skewed domain experts. The authors read both as polysemanticity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Coarse units (dense MLP neurons, few MoE experts) show less domain-exclusive specialization than very fine-grained experts.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the domain-masking results. The paper acknowledges that its expert-selection criteria are basic. Domain-specific removal results do not isolate capacity pressure as the cause of specialization; the stated comparison to neuron specialization is not extracted as individual rows here.
record.rows_left_out: Other-domain average changes in Tables 11 and 12, OLMoE and LLaMA comparison results in Tables 13 and 14, language masking, toxicity purging, qualitative expert examples, and benchmark performance results were not extracted. These analyses do not directly test the versions represented by the retained rows, or were omitted to prioritize the domain-masking results.

untested.parts: No toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
Does not manipulate capacity or feature importance. Neuron polysemanticity is not measured as a function of capacity.
Does not measure how features spread across neurons, or how well SAEs recover features in the LLM.
Does not test SAE feature completeness, stability or canonicity. Only the cost of SAE reconstruction is shown.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked the rows to V2 and V4, but all rows are the paper's own method or its baselines in an unlearning-selectivity comparison. The study is reclassified as T4, uses_without_test, and no verdicts are given. Superposition appears only as motivation.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network experiments, overlap geometry, near-orthogonality, or sparsity-dependent transition is tested.
The paper examines specialized experts and contrasts them with neuron-level specialization, but does not manipulate capacity or feature importance to test the proposed causal competition mechanism.
The paper does not test whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
Domain-specific SAE-feature suppression is evaluated, but the paper does not test the broad claim that features in ordinary LLMs are generally distributed across many neurons.
The paper does not establish whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
The paper does not measure whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

rows.subject: MONET-1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Removed experts assigned to the named MMLU domain using routing-score skewness; reports target-domain accuracy change.
rows.note: The paper reports selective domain knowledge unlearning; this outcome does not by itself establish that capacity pressure caused specialization.
rows.check: Own-method result (MONET expert removal, Table 11), not a measure of capacity-driven polysemanticity. Unlinked from V2.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MONET-1.4B, all 14 tested MMLU domain masks
reader_labels.reason: Removing experts assigned to a domain reduces that domain's score in every reported condition, consistent with specialization, though it does not establish capacity competition as the cause (r1-r14).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Gemma 2 2B with Gemma Scope SAE, 13 domain masks with target-score decreases
reader_labels.reason: Suppressing domain-assigned SAE features lowers target-domain MMLU accuracy in the reported conditions (r15-r16, r18-r28).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Gemma 2 2B with Gemma Scope SAE, Chemistry mask
reader_labels.reason: The Chemistry target score changes by 0.01, so the reported target-domain result does not show a decrease (r17).
